summary: Under rigid individual identity and classical accessibility, an existent concrete bearer outside all contingent concreta is logically equivalent to a necessarily existing concrete individual; the causal predicate itself is not needed for this step. A two-world structured countermodel has a possible external causal origin of contingent concrete reality and a necessary source, yet one actual contingent individual is uncaused in the other world. Thus the weak modal causal-opportunity candidate is not unrestricted PSR and can eliminate brute-only worlds under its open possibility premises, but it does NOT logically eliminate all actual contingent brute roots. A separate brute-only model with a possible totality beginning but no external possible cause witnesses why the causal-opportunity premise itself is substantive. In this relation-relative formal interpretation, none of the models verifies metaphysical possibility or a particular theory of divine causation.
blocker: Defend, using independent modal/causal evidence rather than merely failure to find contradiction, the possibility that the first obtaining of the totality of contingent concreta could have an external concrete cause; additionally, any attempt to exclude contingent brute ROOTS in actual reality needs a stronger actuality/existential-grounding principle not supplied by modal causal opportunity. Pin and read sources before historical attribution.
